description: The AIJ UWE benchmark datasets are wind tunnel measurements of flow around buildings, prepared by the Architectural Institute of Japan as reference cases for validating computational fluid dynamics of the urban wind environment. In 2025 the authors (Yoshihide Tominaga of Niigata Institute of Technology, Hideki Kikumoto of the University of Tokyo, Tsubasa Okaze of Institute of Science Tokyo and co-authors) published four cases on Zenodo: Case A, a single 1:1:2 building; Case B, a 1:4:4 building; Case C, a 3 by 3 array of blocks with the centre building at three heights and wind speeds at pedestrian height; and Case D, a high-rise within low-rise city blocks for several wind directions. Each record holds approach-flow profiles, velocity and turbulence measurements, plots of measurement points and a readme; Case D also gives the building geometry as STL. Access: open download from Zenodo. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: scale-model idealised geometries, not real sites; the original experiments are older papers cited in each record. Simulation uses are CFD validation for pedestrian wind comfort and safety around buildings and in public spaces, and wind-load and ventilation studies. Related records: the NEES wind-excited benchmark building loads.
